visual_base.visual_narrative_log: (1) A man wearing a blue baseball cap and a black Air Jordan T-shirt stands in a modern, brightly lit kitchen with white cabinets. He speaks directly to the camera with an expressive face, using hand gestures to explain his daily cooking routine and the mess it creates on the countertop. (2) He demonstrates the specific problem by holding up a yellow Hasegawa cutting board and a metal colander, showing water dripping onto the marble countertop near the sink. He points to a pink cloth and an old white T-shirt he has been using as makeshift absorbent mats next to a black knife rack. (3) The man introduces two new products in plastic packaging: a grey sponge absorbent mat and a beige diatomaceous earth mat. He compares their physical sizes and textures, showing the sponge one is significantly larger and more flexible than the smaller, rigid-looking diatomaceous earth mat while pointing at the price stickers. (4) In a subsequent review scene one month later, the man is wearing a white T-shirt. He demonstrates that the grey sponge mat has become hard and brittle, poking it with his finger to show its stiff state while shaking his head in a warning gesture.

narrative_and_purpose.mainPurpose: The video aims to share a household solution for drying kitchenware by reviewing and comparing two absorbent mats from Nitori, ultimately providing a warning against the sponge-based version after one month of use.
